title: Pre-Purchase Ship Inspection Shenzhen | Yantian & Shekou
description: Pre-purchase inspection in Shenzhen for buyers of container ships, offshore vessels and feeders at Yantian, Shekou, Chiwan and the western anchorages.
h1: Pre-Purchase Inspection in Shenzhen: Container Ships at Yantian, Offshore Vessels and Feeders in the West
intro: In Shenzhen the right plan for a buyer's inspection depends first on which side of the city the ship is on. At Yantian, mainline container ships stay only for their scheduled working time, so a buyer sees a focused slice of a young, heavily loaded ship. In the western port around Shekou, Chiwan and Mawan, feeders wait for berths, offshore vessels lie at base between charters and ships dock for repair, and there is time to look properly. Atlantis sends its team from India to either side, with Chinese visas arranged against the viewing date.

highlights.p: Supply and support vessels serving the South China Sea fields lie at western-port bases when they are off contract. A buyer can see the cargo deck, liquid mud and fuel tanks, winches and machinery with time to spare, because the vessel is not working.

highlights.h: Container ships seen in their berth window
highlights.p: At Yantian the call is planned to the hour and cargo work continues throughout. The visit targets what matters on a young, large container ship: coaming tops, hatch corners, lashing bridge supports, scrubber lines and the engine room, agreed with the buyer before arrival.

Many ships seen in Shenzhen are managed, financed or bought from Hong Kong, a short crossing away. The buyer's superintendent can attend from either city, but the team needs a Chinese visa for Shenzhen work, which is the longest item in the plan.

sections.h: Yantian or the western port: where can a buyer inspect a ship in Shenzhen?
p: Yantian International Container Terminals, in the east, handle large ships on the Asia–Europe and transpacific trades. A buyer's inspection there is a single berth call with cargo on board, so the agreed list goes no further than deck, coamings, lashing structure, accommodation, engine room and any scrubber system. The crane plan sets the order: the team works on the parts of the deck the cranes are not using at that moment.

The western port offers more. Feeders and regional container ships at Shekou and Chiwan sometimes stay long enough to release ballast tanks; offshore vessels at their bases between contracts can open most of their tanks; ships at the Shekou repair facilities may be in dock with the bottom visible; and the anchorages off the western port hold ships in ballast waiting for berths, yard slots or the completion of a sale.
list: Yantian International Container Terminals: deck, coamings, lashing bridges, engine room and scrubber lines within the berth window
Shekou and Chiwan terminals: feeders and regional container ships, with ballast tanks on longer stays
Offshore vessel bases in the western port: tanks, cargo deck and machinery on vessels off contract
Shekou repair facilities: dry hull and open tanks when a seller docks before delivery
Western anchorages: ships in ballast waiting for berths, yard slots or the sale to close

sections.h: Buying an offshore supply or support vessel in Shenzhen
p: Offshore vessels change hands often, and the South China Sea fleet based in the western port is no exception. A buyer is taking on a ship whose cargo deck has carried pipe, containers and equipment in open water, whose tanks have held liquid mud, brine, base oil, drill water and fuel, and whose machinery has run long hours on station. The inspection is shaped around those uses.

On deck, plating is gauged where cargo has been dragged and dropped, the crash rails and their supports are examined, and on anchor-handling vessels the stern roller area and towing pins are checked for wear and cracking where the seller allows a patch to be cleaned. Liquid mud tanks are the hardest to judge, because residue hides the steel; the seller should clean at least one for entry if the buyer wants it seen. Chain lockers, fuel tanks and the engine room complete the picture.

Machinery readings cover the generators, thruster drives and pumps the chief engineer can run alongside. Station-keeping systems and dynamic positioning trials are outside the scope: the report records only what was seen and measured, and refers the buyer to the vessel's own trial and maintenance records for the rest.

sections.h: What can a buyer learn about a large container ship during a Yantian call?
p: Large container ships calling at Yantian are usually young, so general hull wastage is rarely what decides the purchase. The questions are local: are the hatch coaming tops and corners sound after years of heavy stacks, are the lashing bridge supports cracked, has the scrubber wash-water piping thinned at bends and valves, and do the generators and pumps run cleanly? Each of those can be answered, at least in part, within a berth call.

Mainland rules restrict open-loop scrubber discharge in some waters, so the system may be idle or on closed loop during the call, which gives the team access to the piping. Ballast tanks are entered only if the master can release them safely while cargo work continues. The buyer receives a focused report of what was reached, with a plain list of what a single call did not allow.

sections.h: When the seller docks the ship at Shekou before delivery
p: A seller sometimes docks the ship before handing her over, for a survey, a repair or bottom work agreed in the negotiation. For the buyer, a docking at the Shekou repair facilities is the best view available: the bottom shell, sea chests, rudder and propeller area are dry, tanks are often open and staging may already be up.

The visit is timed with the yard's programme, so the team arrives after the hull has been washed but before new coating covers the steel. Readings on the bottom plating and at the sea chests, and crack checks at known details, are then taken on bare or lightly coated steel, and the report keeps the condition found apart from the repairs the yard is carrying out.

Cruise ships also dock at Shekou, and the occasional buyer of an older cruise ship can see sewage, grey-water, ballast and sea-water piping and tanks there in a way that no turnaround call would allow.

sections.h: Hong Kong buyers, Chinese visas and planning a Shenzhen visit
p: Ships calling at Shenzhen are often managed from Hong Kong, and the buyer's superintendent or broker may cross the boundary for the day. The Atlantis team, travelling from India, needs a Chinese visa issued against an invitation letter, and Hong Kong entry as well if it routes through Hong Kong International Airport. Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport is the direct route and avoids the crossing.

Terminal passes and escorts at Yantian and the western terminals, launches to the anchorages, and gate passes with safety induction at the repair facilities are arranged by the seller's agent or the yard. A ship that calls on both sides of the boundary can be inspected by two administrations within days, so reading her port state control record under the Tokyo MoU before boarding is worthwhile; it shows where earlier inspectors found fault.

Readings from the visit belong to the buyer's decision. Class accepts thickness measurement towards its surveys only from firms holding UR Z17 approval from the ship's society, and Atlantis is still working towards that approval with DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS.

vessels: Bulk carriers waiting off the western port
codes: Norwegian Saleform (NSF 2012) Clause 4 – inspection by the buyers
IACS UR Z7 – hull classification surveys and coating condition
MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14 – sulphur limits and scrubber operation
deliverables: Findings matched to the side of the port and the access the call allowed
Deck, coaming and lashing support findings with located photographs
Spot thickness readings on deck, in tanks and on bottom plating where reached
Offshore vessel cargo deck, tank and stern area condition
Machinery vibration and thermal readings, and the items left uninspected

faqs.q: Can you inspect an offshore supply vessel at its Shenzhen base before purchase?
faqs.a: Yes. Vessels lying at western-port bases between charters are well suited, because they are not working and can release tanks for entry. Ask the seller to clean at least one liquid mud tank if the buyer wants its steel seen, and to have the chief engineer available to run the generators, thruster drives and pumps for readings.

faqs.q: How much can a buyer see of a container ship at Yantian?
faqs.a: A focused part. The ship keeps to her berth window with cargo work under way, so the visit covers hatch coaming tops and corners, lashing bridge supports, the reachable deck plating, scrubber piping and the engine room. Holds are not entered. If the buyer needs more, a later call at the western port or a docking may give it.

faqs.q: Can a Hong Kong buyer's superintendent join the inspection in Shenzhen?
faqs.a: Yes. The superintendent can cross from Hong Kong for the day and work alongside the team, agreeing priorities on board. The Atlantis team needs a Chinese visa for Shenzhen work, so please send the vessel name, the side of the port and the expected dates to info@atlantisndt.com as early as possible.

faqs.q: Do you check dynamic positioning systems on offshore vessels?
faqs.a: No. Dynamic positioning trials and station-keeping performance are outside the inspection. The team records the condition of structure, tanks, deck equipment and running machinery, and notes the DP records the seller makes available, but any assessment of the DP system itself needs a specialist whom the buyer appoints separately, ideally timed to the same visit.

faqs.q: Is it worth waiting for the ship to dock at Shekou before inspecting her?
faqs.a: If the sale terms allow, often yes. A docking shows the bottom shell, sea chests and stern area dry, and tanks may be open with staging in place. The catch is timing: the docking may fall after the inspection period in the memorandum, so the buyer and the brokers should decide early whether to inspect afloat, wait, or do both.

faqs.q: Can the inspection cover a ship anchored off the western port?
faqs.a: Yes. Ships in ballast waiting off the western port for berths, yard slots or the completion of a sale can be reached by launch through the seller's agent. Holds and ballast tanks can be prepared for entry, and the generators run for machinery readings. The anchorage period is often the longest quiet time a trading ship offers in Shenzhen.
